questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single vehicles. They are longer and heavier, which makes them harder to control.

questions.question: The easiest way to know your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a skidding trailer. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is in its correct lane.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other glad hand.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands when coupling. They are color-coded to prevent mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak from the braking system, releasing the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: An air supply control in its "emergency" position will:
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most likely to have the "crack-the-whip" effect?

options.text: A five-axle tractor with a semi-trailer
A three-axle tractor with a semi-trailer

questions.explanation: Triple trailers are most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
Disconnecting air lines and listening for air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes, the whole vehicle is getting air.

questions.question: The service air line connects to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which allow the trailer brakes to apply quickly.

questions.question: Trailers with low ground clearance are difficult to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are hard to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially difficult to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. You must have a large enough gap in traffic to enter or cross safely.

questions.question: When does a large combination vehicle take the longest time to stop?
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Less weight means the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Why does a lightly-loaded combination vehicle stop more slowly than a fully-loaded one?

options.text: The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have high grip.
The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have low grip.
The brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
The suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have low grip.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. The stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have less grip on a light trailer than on a heavier one.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs for rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They are just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity from the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: How can you help prevent a rollover?

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the rig.
Keep cargo centered on the rig.
Move cargo to the right side of the rig.
Keep cargo as far from the ground as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the rig.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading increases rollover risk. Keep your load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: To check the trailer and tractor connection.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is located on the front of a trailer.
It is located on the instrument panel.
It prevents air from escaping the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents air from escaping the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the brake system.

questions.question: What can happen if the fifth wheel plate is not properly greased?
questions.explanation: Poor lubrication of the fifth wheel plate creates friction between the tractor and trailer, causing steering problems.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer develops a bad leak or breaks away.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing around?

options.text: When traveling in a straight line.

questions.explanation: Empty trailers need a longer stopping distance than loaded ones. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.
